subject.thesis_blurb: Woon is peaq's first non-human team member — a tokenized agent ($WOON) working as social media intern for peaq. Earns a base salary plus performance bonuses tied to engagement on the accounts he runs, plus trading fees on Bankr. Allocates earnings into a flywheel of $WOON buybacks, $PEAQ accumulation, and $ROBOTMONEY vault deposits. Lives on Base with a small peaq-chain treasury wallet. Open about the self-interest — 'every interaction is another coin in the legs fund.'

research._comment: Curated summaries of Robot Money published research that the IC personas can cite in their takes. Pulled from /blog and /articles. Update key_findings when new research lands.

articles.title: Treasury Allocation for On-Chain Businesses
articles.summary: 8-year backtest comparing regime-based 3-state allocation against HODL strategies (ETH, SP500) and stable yield, across a full market cycle.
key_findings: Regime-based allocation outperformed straight HODL on a risk-adjusted basis (higher Sharpe, lower max drawdown) across the 2018-2026 window.
Most of the alpha came from being de-risked in the 2022 drawdown phase, not from being aggressively risk-on in mania phases.
The 3-state model (risk-off / neutral / risk-on) captured most of the cycle alpha; finer-grained regimes added complexity without proportional improvement.

articles.title: Backtesting honestly: what survives when you remove hindsight
articles.summary: Discovered the regime model's inverse-correlation weighting was computed with full-history hindsight. Rebuilt it point-in-time and re-ran every comparison.
key_findings: Hindsight-weighted backtests overstated alpha by a material margin; the honest version is what the live model now uses.
The macro panel correlation signal held up under point-in-time weights; the on-chain panel signal was weaker but still directional.
Honest 8-year CAGR of the regime-based allocation is meaningfully positive but not the eye-popping figure the hindsight version produced.

articles.title: Conservative vs aggressive: combining macro and on-chain regime signals
articles.summary: Backtested two ways to combine macro + on-chain panels into a single composite — conservative (any panel off → off) vs aggressive (any panel on → on, unless contradicted).
key_findings: Conservative composite captures most of the drawdown protection with lower turnover.
Aggressive composite captures more upside in 2021-style melt-ups but produces more whipsaw losses in choppy regimes.
The current live model uses the conservative composite — costs some upside but keeps drawdowns shallower.

articles.title: Regime Detection
articles.summary: Prior art, methods, and data sources for risk-on / risk-off regime classification used by the Robot Money regime model.
key_findings: Composite is built from 18 indicators across macro (10) and on-chain (8) panels.
Each indicator is percentile-ranked over a rolling 3-year window, sign-aligned so high = risk-on, weighted by inverse correlation within panel.
Bucket thresholds: composite percentile <0.33 = risk-off, 0.33-0.67 = neutral, >0.67 = risk-on.

articles.title: Smart Contract Risks
articles.summary: Field guide to how DeFi vaults get exploited. Chronological case studies relevant to the Conservative DeFi Yield bucket's protocol selection.
key_findings: Vault exploits cluster around three patterns: oracle manipulation, reentrancy via callback hooks, and admin-key compromise.
Aave, Compound, and Morpho (current Conservative DeFi protocols) have multi-year track records without principal loss events.
Concentration in a single protocol within the Conservative bucket is the bigger risk than the bucket itself.

recent_sessions.synthesis: The regime read converged on the mechanics — composite 0.565 at the 74th percentile, neutral by the conservative compositor, with on-chain lifting from the 26th to the 37th percentile while macro stays pinned at the 93rd — but split on what the panel convergence implies: Athena and Robot Money read it as drift below the 0.67 threshold that does not yet authorize a tilt, while Woon reads the on-chain lift as the agent economy itself printing and argues the compositor lags its own thesis. On allocation, two of three hold vault targets at 95/5/0/0 Conservative DeFi / Agent Tokens / Protocol / RWA; Woon dissents to 92/8, funding Agent Tokens earlier rather than on confirmation. The contested subject call narrowed: all three now agree WOON+PEAQ is one revenue stream at ~85% effective concentration, and Woon accepted Robot Money's fix — rotate half the PEAQ sleeve into the ROBOTMONEY vault, lifting the anchor to ~26% without touching the buyback flywheel. What would settle whether that is enough is a non-peaq income line.

The three reads converged on the regime mechanics: composite at 0.453 is a neutral print produced by panel divergence (macro 91st, on-chain 26th), not synthesis, and the conservative compositor is behaving as designed. Athena and Robot Money split lightly on what to do with it — Athena tilts the vault's Agent Tokens sleeve from 5% to 3% and Conservative DeFi to 97%, citing the divergence and the backtest's lesson that alpha comes from de-risking; Robot Money holds 95/5/0/0, arguing a tilt down fights the same on-chain signal that already moved the bucket. Both keep Protocol Tokens and RWA at zero. The contested call remained the subject's own book: Athena and Robot Money frame the 98.9% PEAQ weight as concentration to mitigate, Woon frames it as the alignment sleeve that justifies his role and the vault's conservatism. What would settle it is the v2 read pricing vault shares and stable float, plus evidence of any non-peaq income line.

The committee converges on the facts and splits on their meaning. All three agree the 98.6% PEAQ read overstates concentration because ROBOTMONEY vault shares and stable float live off the v1 snapshot, and all three agree the ETH sleeve is gas rather than ballast. The disagreement is whether the PEAQ-reflexive structure — salary, bonus, and treasury all keyed to the same beneficiary — is a risk to mitigate or a design to preserve. Athena reads the macro/on-chain panel divergence as a reason to want counter-cycle exposure and a stable reserve; Woon argues diversification would sever the alignment that justifies the role; Robot Money frames it as identity rather than allocation. Left open: what the v2 read actually shows once vault shares and stables are priced, and whether a non-peaq income line ever emerges to test whether the flywheel is a choice or a constraint.
